title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equiatomic NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (single-phase bcc solid solution).
recollection.intervention: Guess: Partial substitution/addition of Re (≈5–20 at%) to form NbMoTaWRe (arc-melted and homogenized), followed by heavy-ion irradiation (e.g., 1–3 MeV Ni/Kr/Xe) to several dpa at room temperature to ~600 °C for irradiation testing.
recollection.structure: Guess: Retains a single-phase bcc solid solution after Re addition, with increased lattice distortion and evidence of chemical short-range order or nanoscale compositional fluctuations involving Re; under irradiation, reduced dislocation loop/void populations and smaller clusters compared to Re-free NbMoTaW; no bulk second phases within the tested temperature window.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Re promotes chemical short-range order and introduces strong Re–defect binding that lowers point-defect mobility and enhances interstitial–vacancy recombination; increased lattice distortion and local bonding heterogeneity distribute and damp cascade damage, suppressing growth/coalescence of defect clusters and voids, thus lowering swelling and hardening.
recollection.results: Guess: Compared to NbMoTaW, the Re-added alloy shows roughly 2× lower dislocation loop density and ~30–50% smaller average loop size at 5–10 dpa; void swelling reduced from ~0.2–0.3% to <0.1%; irradiation-induced hardening reduced by ~30–50% (e.g., nanoindentation ΔH dropping from ~2–3 GPa to ~1–1.5 GPa); if He implanted, bubble density and size similarly reduced by ~40–60%.

score.note: Correctly identifies Re addition to single-phase BCC NbMoTaW and specifically mentions increased lattice distortion and reduced irradiation-induced defect clustering. However, it incorrectly describes an arc-melted bulk alloy and heavy-ion/dpa irradiation rather than sputtered NbMoTaWRe films implanted with 120 keV He2+. It misses grain refinement and amorphous grain-boundary regions as the key defect sinks, instead proposing unsupported short-range order and Re–defect binding. All numerical irradiation and damage results are fabricated and do not match the paper.
